consumer-conformance-record.text: As an integrator, I can read the registration, holding update, termination, reading and shared-publication requirements and see which comparisons have evidence. The sixteen requirements are published in the generated evidence page. Every requirement is uncovered: no executable comparison with the application-held model exists yet.

Seven requirements compare the previous and application-held designs. Their old side is computed from the retained Lean model. The development-network journey and refusal jobs are separate observations; they establish the transactions they run and do not establish agreement with the model.

reading-from-a-registry-address.text: As a reader, I give a registry address and key without a signer, blueprint or local registry state. Four requirements describe the neutral key status, open datum's live holding and pending termination, measured provider calls, rows and bytes with another registry's holdings at the same address, and named refusals. They are published uncovered: no executable comparison with the application-held model backs these reading requirements yet.

The registration journey runs both packaged readers at connected live, pending and terminal checkpoints and reads an unused key. Its artifact includes the answers and a known-key query measurement. The registration refusals job runs wrong-network, unknown-policy and failed-provider reads beside passing controls. These are separate command observations, with controls that reject altered answers; they establish nothing about agreement with the model. See reading a key for the commands and settings, and the generated evidence page for receipt-derived standings.

creating-on-shared-publications.text: Five requirements describe a later creation reusing both scripts, an independent creator reusing them from the chain, separation between application releases, registration in a registry created on shared copies and measured creation costs. They use the existing inventory convention and remain uncovered for the same reason as the preceding requirements: no executable comparison with the application-held model exists yet. The seven comparison rows and four reading rows keep their previous contents and standings.

The registration journey, recovery partitions and checked measurement receipts are separate evidence boundaries. They show the packaged commands and measured transactions they run and nothing about agreement with the model. An executable conformance language for creation claims is outside this change. The reuse guide shows the commands and discovery receipt fields; the cost comparison reads its figures from receipts.

read-the-evidence.text: The inventory carries a coverage plan. Only validated receipts for the stated revision can establish execution. The generated page leaves requirements without those receipts visible as uncovered. Its marked appendix preserves the generic backend-contract snapshot with its original code revision and source provenance; those results do not cover the comparison requirements.

check-the-reader.text: The appendix tests check the evidence reader. The coverage ratchet reports regressions against its protected base. Neither command supplies the missing model comparisons. The aligned models remain at the application-held model and the open-datum model.
